math: \bar y_0=0,\quad\bar y_t=\frac1t\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}y_i\ (t>0);\quad p_c(t)=\begin{cases}c&t=0\\\bar y_t&t>0\end{cases};\quad F((n,m),z)=\left(n+1,m+\frac{z-m}{n+1}\right);\quad S_c(0)=(0,c),\ S_c(t+1)=F(S_c(t),y_t);\quad S_c(t)=(t,p_c(t))
plain: The all-time mean successor identity has positive real denominator t+1. At t=0 the empty empirical mean is0 but the actual prediction is c. The first recursive update cancels c and gives (1,y0). For t>0 induction and the proved mean successor identity give the complete state identity. Existing decomposition, minimization and uniqueness prove the positive-prefix mean is the actual hindsight squared-loss leader; interval feasibility makes it an admissible comparator. The prediction uses the previous prefix, rather than an argmin or state oracle.

contract.model: Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. Fix initial c before observations. Lean time t counts observed labels y0,...,y(t-1); predict before observing yt, then update the local state with yt.
contract.assumptions: The algebraic identities hold for all real initial values and labels. Source feasibility requires c in [0,1] and only the strict-past labels yi in [0,1] for i<t; the current and future labels are unrestricted.
contract.parameters: The state is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair (count,value). The count grows; there is no fixed-bit memory, executable implementation or runtime certificate. Strict-prefix equality compares the same fixed c and gives no causality guarantee if an external caller chooses c from future data.
contract.regret: The exact half specialization connects this same recursive trajectory to existing source regret bounds. Arbitrary c has no new quarter or rate theorem here.
contract.guarantee: The all-time mean successor identity has positive real denominator t+1. At t=0 the empty empirical mean is0 but the actual prediction is c. The first recursive update cancels c and gives (1,y0). For t>0 induction and the proved mean successor identity give the complete state identity. Existing decomposition, minimization and uniqueness prove the positive-prefix mean is the actual hindsight squared-loss leader; interval feasibility makes it an admissible comparator. The prediction uses the previous prefix, rather than an argmin or state oracle.
